CODE
Art. 2.3.40. 
Withdrawal of powers of management 
If one of the spouses demonstrates ineptitude in the management of both the common patrimony and his own patrimony or jeopardises the interests of the family, his spouse may request that all or part of his powers of management be withdrawn.
The family court may entrust this management either to the applicant or to a third party designated by it.
This decision may be revoked if the reasons which justified it cease to exist.
Any court decision withdrawing or restoring to one of the spouses his or her powers of management is communicated, when this decision has become res judicata, by the clerk of the court which rendered the decision to the central register of matrimonial agreements.
If the spouse to whom the management is withdrawn or returned exercises an independent professional activity for which he or she must be registered with the Crossroads Bank for Enterprises, the clerk of the court informs the Crossroads Bank for Enterprises.
Article 1250 of the Judicial Code applies (publicity of protective measures: Any decision ordering a protective measure, terminating it or amending it shall, at the registrar's request, be inserted by extract in the Moniteur belge. The same applies to a foreign protection measure that has been recognised or declared enforceable that orders, modifies or terminates a foreign protection measure referred to in Article 3, a) to d), f) and g) of the Hague Convention of 13 January 2000 on the International Protection of Adults, taken in a State that is a party to the Convention or for a protection measure similar to those listed in this Article, taken in a third State with regard to a person of full age, recognised by the justice of the peace.]
Publication shall be made within fifteen days of the decision ordering the protection measure, terminating or amending it [or recognising or rendering enforceable a foreign protection measure referred to in paragraph; the officials to whom the omission or delay is attributable shall be held liable to the persons concerned if it is proven that the omission or delay was the result of collusion.
